sehemu: Part II: Consolidated Fund and Finances of the United Republic
jina: Removal of the Controller and Auditor-General from office
maudhui: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Article, the Controller and Auditor-General of the United Republic shall be obliged to vacate office upon attaining the age of sixty years or such other age as may be prescribed by a law enacted by Parliament. (2) The Controller and Auditor-General may be removed from office only for inability to perform the functions of his office (either due to illness or to any other reason) or for misbehaviour or for violating the provisions of the law concerning the ethics of public leaders, and shall not be removed from office except in accordance with the provisions of subarticle (4) of this Article. (3) If the President considers that the question of removing the Controller and Auditor-General from office needs to be investigated, then in that event the following procedure shall apply— (a) the President shall appoint a Special Commission which shall consist of a Chairman and not less than two other members, and the Chairman and at least half of the other members of such Special Commission shall be persons who are or have been Judges of a High Court or of a Court of Appeal in any country within the Commonwealth; and (b) the Special Commission shall investigate the matter and make a report to the President on the facts and shall advise the President whether or not the Controller and Auditor-General should be removed from office on the grounds of inability to perform his functions due to illness or any other reason or on grounds of misbehaviour. (4) If the Special Commission appointed in accordance with the provisions of subarticle (3) of this Article advises the President that the Controller and Auditor-General be removed from office, then the President shall remove him from office. (5) If the question of removing the Controller and Auditor-General from office has been referred to a Special Commission for investigation pursuant to the provisions of this Article, the President may suspend the Controller and Auditor-General from duty, and the President may at any time rescind the decision to suspend him, and in any case such decision shall cease to have effect if the Special Commission advises the President that the Controller and Auditor-General should not be removed from office. (6) A person who is or has been the Controller and Auditor-General shall not be appointed to or hold any other office in the service of the Government of the United Republic. (7) The provisions of this Article shall not apply to a person appointed to act as Controller and Auditor-General.

(3) If the President considers that the question of removing the Controller and Auditor-General from office needs to be investigated, then in that event the following procedure shall apply— (a) the President shall appoint a Special Commission which shall consist of a Chairman and not less than two other members, and the Chairman and at least half of the other members of such Special Commission shall be persons who are or have been Judges of a High Court or of a Court of Appeal in any country within the Commonwealth; and (b) the Special Commission shall investigate the matter and make a report to the President on the facts and shall advise the President whether or not the Controller and Auditor-General should be removed from office on the grounds of inability to perform his functions due to illness or any other reason or on grounds of misbehaviour.

(4) If the Special Commission appointed in accordance with the provisions of subarticle (3) of this Article advises the President that the Controller and Auditor-General be removed from office, then the President shall remove him from office.
